content.content: When opening a draft for a node, the deccy CLI shall create the draft's jj workspace at the change that owns that node, so that the workspace's working copy holds the node's owned set as the record's base records it.
content.rationale:
One requirement fixes the revision a draft's jj workspace is created at, and it fixes it at the change that owns the draft's node. Where the workspace goes is already answered (lpkssxpp), so what the opening still has to settle is which content its working copy starts from, and that is one answer rather than several: a workspace either starts at the node's change or at something that is not that content, and every other candidate is a different answer to the same question. It is written as one sentence because the start and the base agreeing with the workspace are one commitment — a start that the base does not describe is not a start this decision permits.

The base the opening writes is why. A draft's record carries a content-identity base of its node's owned set, an entry per owned path taken from the content as it is read at the change that owns it, and the draft's edits are made in its workspace against that owned content as it stood when the workspace and its record were made (qrqsxyzz). The base is therefore a statement about one specific content: the owned set at the change that owns the node. For that statement to describe the workspace it guards, the workspace must be created at exactly that change, and there is exactly one such change, because a node has one change and that change is where its document and refs are read from. Created anywhere else, the workspace would hold content the base does not describe while the base describes content the workspace does not hold, which is the disagreement qrqsxyzz exists to catch, made at the opening rather than at the landing.

The two prerequisites either side of the revision leave it free and do not compete with naming it. A draft's jj workspace is a working copy of the repository's tree (xqzstoyo): a copy is always a copy of some revision, and that node fixes the kind of thing copied — the repository's tree, not a second tree or a document — while saying nothing about which revision it is copied from. The place is fixed too, and fixed elsewhere: one per-user draft-workspace root outside the repository, at the path inside the repository's own namespace under that root that the record's handle names (lpkssxpp). A path is not a revision: naming the change a workspace is created at says nothing about where the directory goes, and the place says nothing about what the directory starts from. This requirement therefore answers only the question its prerequisites left open, and neither re-derives the place nor re-decides what a working copy is.

The one-node rule makes the answer single. A draft names exactly one node, the node whose content it will change, so the change that owns that node is one change for every draft, named by the draft rather than chosen from its surroundings (znskspqs). Nothing here reads another draft, another record, or the edit the drafts belong to in order to find the start, and no draft's start can move because a second draft exists.

Neither the edit nor the parent of the node's change is that content. The edit is the unit the draft's work belongs to, and it is a unit of review, not a unit of history: one edit carries a draft for each node it touches, so its content is not any one node's owned set (znskspqs). A workspace created at the edit would start from whatever that edit happens to hold — possibly other nodes' work alongside this one's — while the base it must match is a value per path of this node's owned set, read at this node's change (qrqsxyzz); the two would disagree as soon as the edit held anything besides this node's owned set. The parent of the node's change is closer but still the wrong content: it holds the owned set as it stood before that change, so for a node created in its change it holds no node document at all, and for a node changed there it holds the older document and the older refs. The base is read at the change that owns the node, not at its parent, so a workspace started one change earlier would hold content the base does not describe and lack the content it does — the same contradiction one step nearer. The node's change is the only revision at which the owned set is exactly what the base records, which is why it is the only revision the opening may use.

Deliberately not here. Nothing fixes how the CLI causes the workspace to be created at that change: no flag is named, no module, no command and no file, and whether the revision is passed through to the VCS call is left to the implementation that supplies it, which is checked downstream. What this decision settles is the single property the recorded content must hold — a draft's workspace is created at the change that owns the draft's node, so its working copy holds the owned set the record's base records.
